```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

## Problem 1 - Data Import

```{r}
snapshot_files =
  list.files(
    path = "data",
    pattern = "^mcbroken_.*\\.csv$",
    full.names = TRUE
  )

mcbroken_df =
  read_csv(
    snapshot_files,
    na = c("", "NA"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

store_info_df =
  read_csv(
    "data/store_info.csv",
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

state_regions_df =
  read_csv(
    "data/state_regions.csv",
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )
```



```{r}
mcbroken_df =
  mcbroken_df |>
  mutate(
    month = as.Date(str_sub(month, 1, 10))
  ) |>
  left_join(store_info_df, by = "store_id") |>
  left_join(state_regions_df, by = "state") |>
  relocate(
    month, store_id, state, region,
    city, street, longitude, latitude
  )
```

```{r}
data_summary_df =
  mcbroken_df |>
  summarize(
    n_observations = n(),
    n_months = n_distinct(month),
    n_stores = n_distinct(store_id),
    missing_status = sum(
      is.na(active) & is.na(broken)
    )
  )

data_summary_df |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The 12 monthly datasets were combined, and the month variable was converted to a Date. Store information and geographic regions were added using `left_join()`. Missing machine statuses were retained for later investigation.

The resulting dataset contains `r pull(data_summary_df, n_observations)` observations from `r pull(data_summary_df, n_months)` months and `r pull(data_summary_df, n_stores)` unique stores. Important variables include store ID, month, active status, broken status, state, region, and geographic coordinates.

Store counts by state
```{r}
store_counts_df = 
  mcbroken_df |> 
  group_by(state) |> 
  summarize(
    n_stores = n_distinct(store_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  arrange(desc(n_stores))

store_counts_df |>
  summarize(total_stores = sum(n_stores)) |>
  knitr::kable()

store_counts_df |> 
  filter(
    n_stores == max(n_stores) | n_stores == min(n_stores)
  ) |> 
  knitr::kable()
```
```{r}
brokenness_df = 
  mcbroken_df |> 
  filter(active == T) |> 
  summarize(
    n_active = n(),
    n_broken = sum(broken, na.rm = T),
    broken_rate = mean(broken, na.rm = T)
  )

brokenness_df |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

There are in total 13792 stores. TX has the most stores with 1,269 while MP has the lowest 2 stores. Among active machine observations, 21,826 out of 151,113 were reported as broken, corresponding to a brokenness rate of approximately 14.44%. 

## Problem 2 - Exploratory Analysis

```{r}
store_summary_df = 
  mcbroken_df |>  
  group_by(store_id, state, city, street, latitude, longitude) |>
  summarize(
    n_obs = n(),
    n_known = sum(!is.na(active)),
    n_active = sum(active == T, na.rm = T),
    n_inactive = sum(active == F, na.rm = T),
    n_broken = sum(broken == T, na.rm = T),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    inactive_rate = ifelse(
      n_known > 0, n_inactive / n_known, NA_real_
    ),
    broken_rate = ifelse(
      n_active > 0, n_broken / n_active, NA_real_
    )
  )

```

Store with few observations
```{r}
store_summary_df |> 
  filter(n_obs < 9) |> 
  summarize(
    n_stores = n(),
    one_observation = sum(n_obs == 1)
  ) |> 
  knitr::kable()

store_summary_df |>
  filter(n_obs < 9) |>
  arrange(n_obs, store_id) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  select(store_id, state, city, n_obs) |>
  knitr::kable()
```


```{r}
# High activity
store_summary_df |>
  filter(n_obs >= 9, n_known > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(inactive_rate)) |>
  select(store_id, state, city, street,
         n_obs, n_inactive, n_known, inactive_rate) |>
  slice_head(n = 6) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

# High brokenness
store_summary_df |>
  filter(n_obs >= 9, n_active >= 9) |>
  arrange(desc(broken_rate), desc(n_active)) |>
  select(store_id, state, city, street,
         n_obs, n_active, n_broken, broken_rate) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

```

```{r}
# Geographic coordinates
coordinate_outliers_df =
  store_summary_df |>
  filter(
    !(state %in% c("AK", "HI", "GU", "MP")),
    !between(latitude, 24, 50) |
      !between(longitude, -125, -66)
  ) |>
  select(store_id, state, city, street,
         latitude, longitude)

coordinate_outliers_df |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

```

Among 13,792 stores, 239 have fewer than nine observations, including 40 observed only once.Among stores with at least nine observations, the highest inactivity rate was 90% in Windsor Locks, CT, while several stores reported 100% brokenness across 12 active observations. A geographic check identified three implausible mainland coordinates, suggesting potential data-quality issues.
